findings.text: process_started_at duplicates a capability the repository already owns: reckon/crew/gc.py:794 _process_start_epoch already returns a pid's start instant in epoch seconds from /proc/<pid>/stat, and does it correctly. The addition neither extends nor wraps that helper, and because it is called only by the test it adds production surface with no production caller.

The docstring at :128-130 says the fields are split after the closing parenthesis of the comm field, but the code does a naive .split() of the whole line and reads fields[21]; a process whose comm contains a space shifts every later field, so the start instant is wrong for exactly the case the docstring claims to handle (compare gc.py:803-805 and obligation_snapshot._process_stat_fields, which split after the final ')').

The control assertion compares a value the test itself supplied: monkeypatch at :266-270 substitutes started = NOW - 10 days as process_started_at's answer, and _keyed_on_process_age at :232-249 then computes (NOW - started) > 72h, which is arithmetic over the test's own literals and holds whatever the production code does. The genuine guard against the named regression is the following never_read trap at :278-284, and the executed mutation in mutation-process-age.log is what actually demonstrates the case reddens.

`from reckon.crew.admission import service as _service` is now unused (ruff F401): the repair removed the in-test _read_tally block that used it and left the import. The file is new in this node, so this is a finding the node added.

The repair re-adds `parse_utc` to the .shared import, and it has no use in the module (ruff F401); the import was present and unused at the node's base e689315bb7, removed in 8ce5592505, and re-added here, so it is dead code carried in the repair's own hunk rather than a new delta-vs-base finding.

The log the manifest cites for the gate (test_logs: gate.log) contains only its three header lines -- revision, tree, command -- with no pytest summary and no EXIT= sentinel, so '8 passed, EXIT=0' cannot be read from the log named for it; after-suite.log corroborates the result (66 passed including this module, EXIT=0) and negative-control.log restates '8 passed'.
